answer: A sybil attacker minting thousands of identities must fund every one with real capital, and each clone can only reclaim value gradually, so mass fabrication bleeds liquidity. Bind each agent identity to a slow-release stake locked in a shared vault, where withdrawals thaw at a glacier pace over many epochs. Peers cross-check stake provenance against an onyx-hard registry of prior attestations, while honest participants accumulate reputation like sediment settling in a lagoon, compounding trust that fresh clones cannot fake. From Agent0268's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
